title: Introduce data-residency-guards, KMS key scoping, and RBAC v2 role mapping
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Tenant-scoped KMS enforcement and data-residency guards; RBAC v2 mapping now honors region tags; audit header validation for routed requests; migration tool for existing customer KMS bindings.
description: Summary: This PR implements tenant-aware data residency controls (aka 'residency-guards'), scopes KMS key usage to tenant+region, and extends RBAC v2 role mappings to carry region annotations. Motivation: Several enterprise customers requested hard guarantees that keys and audit streams remain in-customer regions and that role grants cannot be used to bypass residency rules. This change closes gaps discovered during compliance reviews and a recent support investigation (SUP-7890). High level changes: 1) Residency guard middleware: routes requests by tenant geo-tag and enforces region pinning policies; rejects or routes to fallback when policy mismatch. 2) KMS scoping: KMS key references now require a tenant and region qualifier; server-side validation added to key lookup path and crypto plugins updated to reject cross-region key usage. 3) RBAC v2 mapping: role mappings accept an optional region_claim attribute which restricts tokens to the specified region; evaluation engine updated to intersect tenant region and role region. 4) Audit propagation: introduced X-Redwood-Audit-Region header enforcement and enriched audit log entries with region and key_id. 5) Migration tooling: included kms-region-migrate script that converts legacy key bindings and emits a report for customer review. 6) Tests & CI: new unit and integration tests including simulated multi-region tenants and negative tests for mis-scoped keys. Commits (high level): - 2a1f7bd: residency guard middleware and policy model - 7b4e2c1: KMS validation and plugin API changes - 9c2d5f8: RBAC v2 evaluator region handling and mapping docs - d45a8e3: audit header enforcement and log enrichment - f1b9c02: kms-region-migrate tool and migration tests - 0e3a91d: add e2e scenarios to private installer suite Changed areas/files (high level): - src/security/residency/guard.go: new middleware and policy loader - proto/policy/residency.proto: policy schema additions - internal/kms/provider.go: key scoping and validation logic (illustrative snippet: if key.Region != request.Region { return ErrRegionMismatch }) - services/authn/rbac/v2/mapping.go: region_claim checks and eval updates - cmd/kms-region-migrate/main.go: migration entrypoint and report exporter - infra/priv-installer/e2e/residency_test.go: e2e scenarios for on-prem installer - docs/security/data-residency.md: design and operator runbook Review notes and conversation: - Priya: "Can we ensure the middleware short-circuits before any key material is fetched?" Author reply: "Yes, guard checks run in the request admission path; added unit test and comment to make ordering explicit." - Luca: "Migration tool looks good, but add a dry-run mode and a CSV report." Author reply: "Added --dry-run and CSV output; report includes before/after key bindings." - Owen: "What happens if a region label is missing on older tenants?" Author reply: "Policy default is inbound: tenants without explicit region remain in 'unscoped' bucket and are blocked from KMS operations until migration; we added an operator-facing migration guide." - Priya requested a security review for crypto plugin changes, later approved after one minor naming nit. CI: initial runs failed on lint due to naming of a test variable; fixed in follow-up commit and all checks passed (unit, integration, e2e). Performance: small runtime overhead for residency checks (~0.6ms median per request in microbench), measured in tests and within SLO for targeted customers. Backwards compatibility: the KMS provider API introduces a non-breaking optional parameter for region; we included shims in legacy adapters. Migration: kms-region-migrate included and tested; migration has to be scheduled by operator and can be rolled back by restoring previous binding snapshot. Security considerations: added threat mitigation section to docs and required an ACL check prior to migration script execution. Merge details: PR approved by reviewers and merged via squash on 2026-03-02. Squash commit message: "security: add data-residency guards, KMS scoping, RBAC v2 region mapping" Follow-ups: - ENG-4821: rollout plan for Dedicated clusters and Private installer upgrades - SEC-134: audit rule to alert on any requests rejected by residency guard - PM-210: UI controls to show tenant region and migration status in console Known limitations: cross-region read-only audit streams are not migrated automatically; operator action required. Notes for release: this change should be rolled out to staging + canary before full prod; include operators on migration schedule. Related: references SUP-7890 and internal design doc link: https://linear.app/redwood/doc/RESIDENCY-DESIGN (internal).
